Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking the time to engage with MedHealth on your platform. As part of our vendor selection we need a focused response on data transfer and contractual safeguards. Can you provide: 

- Your standard DPA annex (including processor obligations and security controls)

I attached a short spreadsheet with our questions to make it easier to map answers. Ideally we get a draft annex and a short write-up by end of week; if you prefer a quick call to align, we can do that too.

Appreciate it — we’re on a tight procurement timeline.

Best,
Elena

MedHealth Systems

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I looped in Marissa (Legal) and Neha (Security & Compliance) so we can consolidate a single response and an annex draft. Quick notes and next steps: 

- We will provide an editable DPA Annex (PDF+redline) and a concise one-page summary of our cross-border transfer approach.
- Short answers to your bullets below — Neha will follow up with control-level detail and current status on DPF self-certification:
  * Cross-border transfers: We support EU SCCs and offer technical/contractual controls; we are also pursuing DPF self-certification (target Q3 2025) and will provide interim mitigations for transfers until certified.
  * Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessors list; for customer workloads we primarily use (provider names redacted in this thread) cloud infra and a managed inference layer. Full list and subprocessors addendum will be attached.

Hi Elena / Priyom — thanks for flagging. Below are consolidated answers intended for procurement/legal review. I attached a draft DPA Annex and a short summary of SCC/DPF posture.

High-level answers (concise):
- DPA Annex: Attached (DPA_Annex_A_redwood_v1.2.pdf). It includes processor obligations, security measures (encryption in transit/at rest, role-based access controls, logging, incident response timelines), and standard breach notification timelines. We can accept customer redlines on most clauses; exceptions are service-specific limitations called out in Section 7.

- Cross-border transfers:
  * Primary contractual mechanism: EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) supplemented by our technical and organizational measures.
  * DPF (US-EU / US-UK): Redwood is actively pursuing Data Privacy Framework self-certification; our current target for completing certification is Q3 2025. Until certification is finalized, we will rely on SCCs + documented technical controls for transfers of personal data to the US.
  * UK transfers: We support UK Addendum to the SCCs where applicable.

- Subprocessors: We maintain a publicly accessible subprocessors register (dynamic list). We use a small set of cloud partners for control plane/metrics and a GPU infra partner for inference workloads. Customers can request a pre-approval/subprocessor assessment for sensitive workloads in Private or Dedicated deployments.

- Data retention & DSARs: Retention is customer-configurable; our hosted default is 30 days for request logs and 90 days for model usage traces (token-level telemetry optional and configurable). We support API-driven DSARs (export, portability, erasure). For enterprise customers we can implement custom retention via policy hooks.

- Security/compliance artifacts: We can share SOC2 Type II summary, architecture diagram, and encryption-in-use docs on an NDA or shared Drive link.

Interim mitigations until DPF certification:
- Encrypt data in transit and at rest with customer-specific keys where required (KMS integrations).
- Restrict access to EU data to EU-based control plane components where possible (Private/Dedicated deployments available).
- Enhanced logging and contractually committed subprocessors list.

If you send any specific redlines, Marissa will coordinate Legal’s response. Happy to join a call to walk controls for your security team.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: DPA_Annex_A_redwood_v1.2.pdf (PDF), SCCs_and_DPF_summary.pdf (PDF)

Thanks Neha — helpful summary. A couple of follow-ups from our legal/security review: 

1) Can you confirm whether token-level telemetry is ever retained longer than the default for debugging / model improvement, and whether customers can opt-out?
2) For SCC reliance today, do you have an executed SCC + technical annex available, or would we need to negotiate the annex?
3) If Redwood completes DPF self-certification before contract signature, are you willing to include a clause committing to migrate transfers to the DPF mechanism and notify customers?

Also, we’ll need a clean, redline-friendly DPA Annex we can circulate internally. Can you send a Word/PDF with change-tracking-friendly formatting?

If possible we’d like proposed language on subprocessors notice timing (e.g., 30 days prior) and on-subprocessor liability carve-outs.

Thanks — I’m available for a short call later today if useful.

Best,
Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medhealth.com>, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 03 Apr 2025 17:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: RFI: DPA annex + cross-border transfer approach

Hi Elena — appreciate the specific asks. Per Neha’s note, attached are: (1) an editable DPA Annex (PDF with redline-friendly formatting) and (2) a short SCC/DPF posture summary. Quick answers inline to your bullets and proposed contract language highlights below.

- Token-level telemetry: Default retention is 90 days for model usage traces; token-level telemetry used for model improvement is opt-in — enterprise customers can opt-out or configure retention to shorter windows. We will update the DPA Annex Section 4.3 to call this out explicitly.

- Executed SCCs / annex: We can provide an executed SCC template plus a technical annex. Typically we include SCC language in the DPA Annex and accept customer redlines on the annex; we do not require negotiating the SCC core clauses in most cases. A draft technical annex is attached.

- DPF commitment language (proposed): "If Redwood completes Data Privacy Framework self-certification prior to the Effective Date, Redwood shall notify Customer within 10 business days and upon Customer request shall enter into an amendment migrating applicable transfers to the Data Privacy Framework mechanism." See Section 9(b) of the attached draft.

- Subprocessors notice timing: Proposed: 30 days prior notice for new subprocessor additions with an opt-out right for sensitive workloads. We propose standard liability carve-outs limited to indemnities for breach caused by subprocessor acts/omissions where Redwood had no contractual ability to obtain equivalent indemnities; we note customers may negotiate stronger liability on a per-deal basis.

Next steps: I can upload the DPA Annex to a shared Drive and produce a DocuSign envelope if you’re ready to circulate internally. Proposed internal timeline from our side: review + redlines by MedHealth this week -> Redwood legal review next 3 business days -> finalize.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/medhealth/DPA_Annex_A_redwood_v1.2
DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/en/rdw/MDH-2025-DPA

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
